goal.title: Finish the first full draft of my master's thesis

nodes.title: Revise and assemble the full draft

events.description: Two weeks of vacation from October 5 to October 18; about 15 hours a week during that time, then back to 4.

conversation.content: I have two weeks off in October and could do maybe 15 hours a week on the thesis during that time. After that it's back to normal.

expected_output.message_to_user:
Two focused weeks are perfect for the literature review — it's the chapter that benefits most from long uninterrupted blocks. Plan: finish chapter 2 during the vacation (about 20 hours), outline chapter 3 section by section (about 5 hours) and, if you do reach 15 hours a week, start writing chapter 3 with what's left. After October 18 you're back to 4 hours a week.
One honest note: at 4 hours a week alone, chapters 2–4 (about 55 hours) would only have been drafted in early January, past the December 10 milestone. The vacation closes that gap rather than creating spare time: with it, the chapters fit by December 10 with about 12 days to spare, and the full draft lands in late December, about 3 weeks before January 15. If the vacation weeks turn out lighter, chapter 3 simply starts after October 18 and the milestone still holds.
